title: What is known about 1RB1LA_1LC1RD_1LA0LC_1RE0RB_1RF1RC_1RA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LA_1LC1RD_1LA0LC_1RE0RB_1RF1RC_1RA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. It belongs to a family of four holdouts that share their first four states, and works as two binary counters, one counting down in the blocks left of the head and one counting up in the gaps right of it. This page lists what is established, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean now proves the counter itself: read the tape as two binary numbers, E in the odd blocks left of the head and N in the gaps right of it, and every countdown of E, for every size of E and N, runs as the counter says (run3, run5). Lean also proves that the blank-tape run enters this counter after 269 steps and runs its first countdown. The pass rules (including the halting one) are proved too.

Coq now reduces the machine to the round map F of busycoq pull request 40 and proves that a halt needs an unmarked round (X odd, every 1 bit of X at an even position). Whether F ever reaches one is open: no invariant keeps the marker. F was iterated 160,000 rounds with no halt and never fewer than 10 marker bits.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: The pass rules
claims.text: Six rules on symbolic tapes, for all values of their parameters and any surrounding tape: a pass on an even top block (L 1 A>0 1^(2k+4) 0^(g+4) 1 R), on a block of 2, on an odd block crossing j small gaps, on a block of 3, a gap of length one closing, and pass_odd_halt: an odd pass whose D-run meets a gap one cell too short reaches F reading a 1, the only halting transition. Proofs by rfl steps and crossing lemmas, written by tools/py/bbtools/symtm.py.

claims.title: The counter, proved for every size
claims.text: Write E in p bits on the left (from the head outward, a 0 bit is 1 1 and a 1 bit is 1 0, above a floor that starts with a 1) and N in n bits on the right (a 0 bit is 0^5, a 1 bit is 0^4 1, followed by any tape X). In mode 3 (top block 1^3) the machine takes (E, N) to (E − k, N + k) for every k ≤ E with N + k < 2n, in at least 26·k steps (run3); in mode 5 (top block 1^5) it takes (E, N) to (E − k, N + 2k) in at least 56·k steps (run5). Proofs: three pass-pair rules written by tools/py/bbtools/symtm.py, the binary decrement and increment on bit lists, and induction on k.

claims.title: The blank-tape run enters the counter
claims.text: After 269 steps from blank tape the machine is in mode 5 with E = 30 (5 bits) and N = 2 (init_counter), and it then counts E down to 0, reaching N = 62 after at least 1680 further steps (first_countdown).

claims.title: A halt needs an unmarked round (Coq, on busycoq's definitions)
claims.text: M1d_needs_unmarked: if halts TM97.tm' c0 (busycoq's halts and c0; TM97.tm' is this table), then some iterate of the round map F from (L, X) = (1, 3) is a round with X odd and div2 X unmarked: no 1 bit at an even position, so every 1 bit of X sits at an even position and X written in base 4 uses only the digits 0 and 1. F and the equivalence of the machine with it (F_spec, eqv_F_gen) are from busycoq pull request 40 by Andrew McKnight (open, not merged; the file is pinned at commit 069dc1e). Added here: F_marker (X odd and div2 X marked: F(L, X) is defined and odd, because F stops at the first even gap of div2 X, and a gap is even exactly when the 1 bit closing it is at an even position), F_None_even (F halts only on even X) and halt_needs_unmarked. The same file proves the statement for 1RB1LA_1LC1RD_1LA0LC_1RE0RB_1RF0LE_1RA---. Print Assumptions: closed under the global context. Coq 8.20.1 on busycoq's BB6 branch (commit 33209bc).

claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 187 cells have been visited and 69 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 2·10<sup>10</sup> steps
Growth shape: exp/fixed
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.081).

claims.title: No halt before 6.03·10<sup>14900</sup> steps
claims.text: The round-2 accelerator py/jump2.py (with c/ps.c, in the folder of 1a), run with the gap encoding of this machine (GB=4 GP=5) and the step constants K3=26,4,10 K5=56,4,10, simulates directly from pass start to pass start until the tape is a counter configuration of lean/Counter.lean, then jumps a whole countdown at once. Each jump is an instance of run3/run5, so its end tape is proved; only the Python reading of the tape, the step count of a jump (the fitted formula) and the direct simulation between jumps are unproved. Every jump of at most 108 steps was re-run by direct simulation and matched token for token. In 45 minutes on one core it made 5,988 jumps and reached step 6.03·1014900 (E up to 49,495 bits) with no halt.

claims.title: Defects stay single
claims.text: In the 15.4 million passes that this run simulated directly (all the transition cascades between its jumps), the right part never held more than one gap of irregular size at a time, never more than 0 blocks of two or more 1s, and the left part never more than two even blocks.

claims.title: The phase transition
claims.text: When E reaches 0 the floor block 1^(2s) under it is popped into the top block, the next pass pushes s single 1s, and a new countdown starts with E = 2s − 1 (s one bits; floor 1^2) in the other mode (3 and 5 alternate); N stays on the right, but the cut leaves a gap of irregular size in front of it. Irregular gaps then act in a cascade of short sub-phases: a gap one too long (for 1a/1b; the analogous residue mod 5 for 1c/1d) collapses into a block 1^2, a gap one too short followed by a single 1 is cut down and passes its defect on to the next gap; sometimes the whole of N is pulled to the left and N restarts at 0. The floor grows by 2 whenever E passes a power of two, so it is about twice the bit length of the largest E so far. Seen at every transition of the runs above; not proved, and no closed formula for the new (E, N) as a function of the old one is known.
claims.where: holdouts/1RB1LA_1LC1RD_1LA0LC_1RE0RB_1RB0RF_0RB---/py/jump2.py (log of the tapes at each counter start)

claims.title: The marker survives 160,000 rounds
claims.text: F iterated from (1, 3) for 160,000 rounds with exact integers: no halt, X odd in every round, and after the fifth round div2 X always has at least 10 one bits at even positions (an unmarked round needs all of them gone at once). L, the length of the left counter, reaches 1.36 million digits. The longest run of rounds whose top gap is odd is 28.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Coq reduces the question to the round map F: the machine halts exactly when F returns None, and that needs a round with X odd and div2 X unmarked (all 1 bits of X at even positions). Each round rewrites the low bits of X, so the marker is not obviously preserved; no invariant proving that it survives every round is known. In 160,000 rounds it never came close (at least 10 marker bits).

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine counts one binary number down and another one up, again and again, in phases that get longer and longer. This page shows the real machine in your browser, explains the two counters, and says exactly where a halt could come from.

facts.text: Proved in Lean, including the only way a pass can halt.
A halt needs a round whose X is unmarked (base-4 digits 0 and 1 only).
No halt in a validated accelerated run (5,988 jumps).

sections.heading: Four machines, one engine
html: Four holdouts share the first four states of this machine, 1RB1LA_1LC1RD_1LA0LC_1RE0RB, and differ only in the last two: 1a 1RB0RF_0RB---, 1b 1RB0RF_1RC---, 1c 1RF0LE_1RA---, 1d 1RF1RC_1RA---. States A to D do almost all of the work; E and F only decide what happens when the head runs into the right part of the tape. This page is about machine 1d; the other three work the same way with different constants.

In 1a and 1b the gaps on the right have lengths 2, 5, 8, 11, ... (3d + 2); in 1c and 1d they have lengths 4, 9, 14, ... (5d + 4). 1a and 1b even agree step for step as long as F only ever reads a 0 followed by another 0, which is what happens in every run we made.

sections.heading: Blocks on the left, gaps on the right
html: Stop the simulator at a moment when the head is in state A on a 0 with a block of 1s to its right. The tape then looks like

Left of the head: blocks of an odd number of 1s separated by single 0s (and one even block at the far left). Right of the head: single 1s separated by gaps whose lengths are 4, 9, 14, .... The odd blocks and the gaps are the digits of two numbers.

sections.heading: How a block of 1s is used up
html: From such a moment to the next (a pass) the head eats the block 1^m two cells at a time: states A, B and C carry one 1 at a time to the left part, then D runs right and writes into the first gap. What happens depends on m:

• m even: two 1s move to the left, the first gap gets one cell shorter;
  • m odd: D runs right over all the gaps of the smallest size, (0^4 1); those gaps are filled with 1s, and the first larger gap is cut;
  • m = 2 or 3: the block merges with the blocks on its left and the head walks back to the 0 left of them.
These pass rules are proved in Lean for every value of the block lengths and every surrounding tape (lean/Rules.lean).

sections.heading: One number counts down, another counts up
html: Read the tape at the start of a pass as two binary numbers. Left of the head, going outward, every pair of cells is one bit of E, lowest bit first: 1 1 is a 0 and 1 0 is a 1, down to an even block, the floor. Right of the head, after the top block, every group of 5 cells is one bit of N: 0^5 is a 0 and 0^4 1 is a 1. (So an odd block 1^(2v+1) is v zero bits and a one bit, and a gap is a run of zero bits closed by a one bit.)

With top block 1^3 (mode 3) one pair of passes subtracts 1 from E and adds 1 to N; with 1^5 (mode 5) two pairs subtract 1 from E and add 2 to N. A pair costs a constant plus 4 steps per trailing zero of E plus 10 per trailing one of N, exactly the work of borrowing and carrying.
This is now proved in Lean for every E and N (lean/Counter.lean: run3, run5), and Lean also proves that the run from blank tape reaches this counter after 269 steps (lean/Init.lean).

sections.heading: When the countdown ends
html: When E reaches 0 the floor 1^(2s) is popped into the top block; the next pass pushes s single 1s, which is E ≈ 2s − 1, all ones, and the mode switches between 3 and 5. N is left on the right, but the pass that cut it leaves a gap of the wrong size, a defect, in front of it.

Defects are worked off in a cascade of short sub-phases: a gap one cell too long collapses into a block 1^2; a block 1^2 followed by a gap makes the next gap one too short; a gap one too short followed by a single 1 is cut and hands its defect to the next gap. Sometimes N is swallowed into the left part entirely and restarts at 0. Then a clean countdown runs again. Since the floor gains 2 cells each time E passes a power of two, the floor is about twice the bit length of the largest E so far, and phases grow fast.

The accelerator py/jump2.py simulates the cascades directly and jumps over every clean countdown with the Lean-proved rule. On this machine it made 5,988 jumps and reached 6.03·1014900 steps without a halt (the first-round accelerator had reached 4.17·1094 steps).

sections.heading: How it could stop
html: The machine halts only when F reads a 1. From a pass start that happens exactly when an odd pass, after the gaps of the smallest size (0^4 1), meets a gap of length two (pass_odd_halt, proved): the D-run stops on it and F reads the 1 behind it. Regular gaps are 4 or 5 cells long (bits 1 and 0 of N), so only a transition can leave such a short gap in that place. (In 1a and 1b the analogous fatal gap has length one and must be followed by a block of two 1s; here any 1 after the gap of two is enough.)

During a countdown there are no defects at all, so a halt can only come inside a transition cascade. In the 15.4 million passes of the cascades of the accelerated run there was never more than one irregular gap at a time, and the fatal gap never appeared in front of an odd pass (the run would have stopped).

sections.heading: The round map and its marker
html: A Coq proof by Andrew McKnight (busycoq pull request 40, open) reads the tape at the start of a round as two numbers: L, the length of the left counter, and X, the right counter, and proves that the machine runs exactly as an explicit map F on (L, X) says, halting exactly when F returns None. F reads the zero gaps between the 1 bits of div2 X from the low end. It stops at the first gap of even length; if every gap is odd it runs out and returns an even X.

A gap is even exactly when the 1 bit that closes it sits at an even position of div2 X. So if div2 X has any 1 bit at an even position (call it marked), F stops early and returns an odd X again, and F can only return None on an even X. This is proved in Coq here (F_marker, M1d_needs_unmarked): a halt needs a round whose X is odd and unmarked, that is, X written in base 4 uses only the digits 0 and 1. Both machines of this pair satisfy the same theorem: 1RB1LA_1LC1RD_1LA0LC_1RE0RB_1RF0LE_1RA--- from (8, 145), 1RB1LA_1LC1RD_1LA0LC_1RE0RB_1RF1RC_1RA--- from (1, 3).
The last rounds: L, the number of 1 bits of div2 X at even positions, and the lowest 32 bits of X (lowest first).

What is open is whether the marker survives every round. A round rewrites the low part of X and pushes new bits on top, and nothing proved so far keeps a 1 bit at an even position of div2 X. In the 160,000 rounds computed the marker never had fewer than 10 bits, while an unmarked round would need every one of the roughly L/2 even positions to be 0 at once.

sections.heading: What is missing
html: The counter is proved; the transitions are not. A transition is a cascade whose course depends on the low bits of E and N and on where earlier defects sit, and no closed formula for the configuration after it is known, in the language of passes. The Coq model above sidesteps this: it describes whole rounds as one explicit map, so the question is now about that map alone. What is missing is an invariant of the map that rules out the halting rounds.
Because the phases grow so fast, simulation can only ever check a few dozen transitions; whatever decides this machine has to be an argument about all transitions at once.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.081).
After 109 steps the tape spans 187 cells (9 left of the start, 172 right), with a density of 1s of 0.369.

The tape (run-length coded, 1^5 is five 1s, C>0 the head in state C on a 0) at some of the last moments the head reached a new cell, cut to 400 characters:

summary: Family 1d: two binary counters, E written in odd blocks left of the head counting down and N written in gaps right of it counting up (proved in Lean for every size); when E runs out the floor block becomes a new E and defects appear on the right; it halts only if two defects meet. No halt to 6.03·10^14900 steps (accelerated run, never more than one defect). Coq: a halt needs an unmarked round of the round map F (PR 40); 160,000 rounds of F keep at least 10 marker bits. Open.
